Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
I haven't actually played a "real" Baali votedeck yet, but I have seen a few over the past year and a half or so.

The idea seems pretty straigtforward: you bring out Annazir, who then Tends his Flock to get Arishat out. You then have 3 table votes plus Arishats cancel special. After Villeining around a bit and Tending more Flocks, Xeper should join the team bringing you up to 6 table votes plus Arishats cancel special. That plus access to Condemnation: Mute should be enough to have votelock on most tables. Proceed to play lots of Reckless Agitations, Stealth and Voter Caps. Mix in some Unleash Hell's Fury, some I am Legion and a Venefictus and you're good to go.

It's a pretty cool deck, no doubt, and can be devastating on the right tables. However, whenever I see someone playing it I'm like "ye or you could just take Marcus Vitel and Lucinde, build a very similar deck and get access to Dominate and Parity Shift.

That said, I did play a votedeck with Arishat and Hordes that didn't do exceptionally good, but was insanely fun to play. I'd basically spend 6 pool to get Arishat out and then used almost MPA to Tend the Flock to a Horde. The Hordes would bleed and get Camera Phones and whatnot and then Arishat called a My Kin Against the World to untap all the Hordes so I could do it all again. Path of Evil Revelations payed for the regular untap and if I didn't have one I'd just leave them untapped after My Kin. The cool thing about the Path is, is that you can play it in your masterphase and then use it immediately to get cheap untaps . That's also why people tend to not remove it. I played tons of votepush to get the My Kin done (Bewitching, Perfect Paragon, Old Friends) and if I didn't have a votercap it kinda fell apart, but ye, that was a fun deck.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
I've been playing and improving a Gr6 Baali vote for a while now.
I do not rely on Tend the Flock because there's no slot for them nor enough MPA, and they force you the get the vampires out in the right order.
I get them out manually (hopefully helped by a Dreams of the Sphinx), Villein them then refill them using Voter Captivation.
Arishat, Xeper and Annazir are usually enough to have the vote lock, but there's 3 Condemnation:Mute out of 75 cards just in case. I also play some Perfect Paragon for its versatility.
Votes are mainly Reckless and Neonate Breach because they are very effective, though the Reckless become useless in 1vs1.
Stealth consist mainly of Lost in Crowds and Swallowed by the Night (for the maneuver), and 2 Elder Impersonation. Combat is mainly Force of Personality (because it cycles well) and Staredown (because it's free).
Bleed defense is not strong (only Archon Investigation), but you should bloat enough using the Voter Cap and Villein to survive.

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
Well ye, sure Unnamed is a pretty good vampire

However, it is also a 10-cap with no title, no inherent +bleed and neither a bounce discipline nor an untap discipline. That's a LOT of "things big vampires need to have to be playable" that Unnamed doesn't have. Oh and she costs a pool to untap.

Also, your "bleed for 3 and gain 3 pool" is, when you account for the cost to untap a "bleed for 3 and gain 2 pool". Let's also not forget that Legal Manipulations and Public Trust both cost a blood (which could be argued is also a pool). Compare her now to Jackie bleeding for 4 and gaining a pool with 2 cards. That's +1 bleed and -1 pool. Jackie's a 3-cap.

I mean, it's NICE, sure, but it´s far from tier1. IMO, you really have to completely dedicate your deck around The Unnamed to make it work. I'm talking Homonculus/Enkil Cog or even Homonculus/Clan Impersonation/Madness Network here. As an example, I played this one for a while and it did reasonably ok against common archtypes:

For the Mages, the same is true; you have to make a deck around it. I have a pretty cool deck with tons of Maureen, Infernal Servitors and Greater Curses that uses all the new toys from HttB. Maureen comes with  as a side-bonus too. Extrala featured it on his blog last year. The thing is, all these cool tricks (except Maybe Unleash, but that is unique) have no place in a vote deck and thus shouldn´t be a reason to play Baali vote.

If you´d ask me, reasons to play Baali vote are
a) Because it's cool
b) Because it's different
c) Because, sure, the Annazir/Xeper/Arishat crypt is damn solid
d) Because you can get votes through without votepush
e) Because they can use Reckless Agitation

There are probably tons more reasons to build a Baali vote deck. Being better than Lucinde/Marcus Vites Parity Shift is not one of them, because frankly, it isn't.

Messages.Author: Kiddo
Messages.Body:
From my experience, if you're going to make a competitive Baali g5-6 vote deck, it is very doable but that deck has to be very focused, which makes it very boring to play (in casual games). There are no room nor time for anything else that isn't either gaining pool via influencing another vamp (Flock, Enchant) or gaining pool via damaging your prey (KRC+voter). IIRC, the only non-boring card I had in a deck was Kaymakli Fragment, and even that card is here to keep you alive.

My point-very efficient deck but I'll never again play it outside tournament...

I made a g5-6 Baali vote deck also, though I haven't had the chance to test it very much so I won't post the whole decklist here. the crypt is fun to play though.

a few gimmicks I used for flavor included Path of The Void, for that extra stealth if needed, and to help Xeper or Annazir who have such amazing built-in actions (hulk SMASH new carthage). Aura of Invincibility to help pile up those permanent votes, it's an overlooked card. Bribes, because the 1 pool pays for the Infernal action, and Arishat can sometimes use her special to deny someone else the poolgain.

edit: now that I think about it, New Carthage popping up everywhere in the metagame is probably the best reason to play this over Ventrue lawfirm.
